weather_report:
Rottnest wakes under a soft lid of grey, the ocean dulled to pewter and the light flattened, kind to the eyes. Through late morning and into the afternoon the sky holds steady in overcast, the sun a pale smudge behind cloud, so brightness is muted and shadows are scarce. UV will be lower than on a blue-sky day, but spring can still bite through the veil; sunscreen and a brimmed hat remain sensible. The air feels gentle and marine, the horizon a little blurred, the day more contemplative than sparkling and still quite pleasant if you like your coast without the glare.

Dress in light layers with something to cut the damp edge if it comes off the water; comfortable shoes if you plan to roam. It’s a good day to roll a bike along the paths without hurry, pause by the salt lakes to listen for bird chatter, or sit by Thomson Bay with a late coffee and watch the water change its shades. If you’re restless, wander up to the lighthouse for a slow look at the muted panorama; if not, find a sheltered bench, open a book, and let the quiet gray do its steady work.
